text.p: Asarco Inc is "optimistic" about exploration work the company is doing for gold in French Guiana and silver in Bolivia, chief executive Richard Osborne said Friday.

Announcing his views to the company's quarterly analysts' meeting, he pointed out Asarco generally is conservative about announcing new projects until reserves are proven and feasibility studies and required permits are in hand.
Exploration Vice President Gerald Van Voorhis described a deposit found in Bolivia (corrects from Chile) as near Serro Rico and Potosi, adding it is amenable to stripping.
He said the company has no partner is this project, adding "we have a lease on the property."
Van Voorhis said "We have (a reserve) estimate, (but) we're not ready to announce it." The company is now doing a feasability study, he added.
Asarco will be ready to announce more in the next six months, Osborne said.
He said the company is "not about to announce (anything about French Guiana) in the next quarter or two."
He described Asarco's 100 percent owned Camp Caiman as the "most advanced" of its projects there.

Osborne said there are no reserve estimates or feasability studies yet for Camp Caiman; and Asarco's joint venture with Guyanor Ressources SA, which is 68 percent owned by Golden Star Resources Ltd, is "some months behind" the wholly owned project.

He told reporters Asarco is in the earliest of stages of a joint exploration venture with Codelco, Chile's state copper company. The venture is looking at a site north of the El Abra mine, owned 51 percent by Cyprus Amax Minerals Co.

Osborne told the analysts the company now expects the Minto Mine in Canada's Yukon Territory to begin production in early 1999, when it is expected to begin producing 26 million pounds of copper annually at a cost of about $0.50 per pound.
He said Asarco has no widescale exploration for lead and zinc worldwide but is looking near its present operations in Missouri, where it would like to expand.
Commenting on the company's worldwide search for gold and silver, he told analysts the precious metals create more value for the company for each dollar of exploration.

Asked about acquisitions, Osborne said the stocks of companies owning gold and silver reserves are too expensive to be attractive, but some of the small gold companies in Australia are offering attractive joint ventures now that the money markets are difficult for them to access.
Speaking to reporters after the analysts' meeting, he said "The U.S. has become one of the more politically unattractive areas of the world" in terms of developing a new mine.
